business_problem: ContextQA wanted to reduce release delays, quality issues, and test flakiness by automating manual software-testing work without requiring customers to write code, while also using enterprise-safe AI models that satisfied privacy and ethics concerns.
solution_summary: ContextQA used IBM watsonx.ai to add generative-AI automation to its no-code testing platform for web, API, and mobile applications. After meeting IBM at SXSW, the company worked with the Build Partner team for a month to evaluate IBM's AI tooling without adding new infrastructure. ContextQA used watsonx.ai and IBM-supplied NLP models to migrate plain-English manual test cases into automated workflows across disparate organizational data, identify what changed in the software under test, and generate relevant suggestions for the next testing actions. The company specifically valued IBM's more controlled and governable model approach compared with alternatives it had tried, because enterprise buyers were sensitive to privacy, ethics, and bias. The result was a practical testing architecture that automates large batches of manual cases, reduces flakiness, and helps ContextQA improve reporting and product quality for larger enterprise customers.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx.ai
solution_components.role: Supplies the NLP and generative-AI capabilities ContextQA uses to convert manual test cases into automated testing workflows and recommendations.

data_flow: Plain-English manual test cases and related organizational data are processed by watsonx.ai and IBM NLP models, which generate automated testing steps and change-aware suggestions that feed ContextQA's testing platform.
business_outcome: ContextQA demonstrated that it could migrate large volumes of manual tests into automated flows within minutes, remove flakiness from testing, and better position its platform for enterprise customers that require trustworthy AI controls.
